subject: EU-only processing: AuroraHealth questionnaire and SCCs scope
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@aurorahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marco Giordano <m.giordano@aurorahealth.com>, Aurora Health Legal <legal@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2029 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: EU-only processing questionnaire - initial ask

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed with procurement and legal, Aurora Health needs written confirmation of the following items to proceed with a pilot:

- Confirmation that all inference and storage for our account will be processed and stored only in EU regions (we're targeting Frankfurt and Dublin).
- Whether the Redwood control plane or any support/ops workflows will result in data leaving the EU (control plane, logs, metadata).
- The scope of the SCCs applied and whether Redwood will sign the new SCCs for in-region processing.
- Operator access: who has remote access to keys/configuration and under what conditions (break-glass, legal process).
- Backup and disaster recovery: where backups are stored, retention windows, and proof-of-deletion process.
- Evidence types you can provide (audit logs, redacted request traces, KMS key ARNs, SOC2 artifact pointers).

I've attached a short questionnaire (Aurora_SCCS_Questions.xlsx) — please return completed. If any of these items require a quick call with your security/privacy team, propose times next week.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — procurement has a 2-week window to finalize terms for the pilot.

Thanks,
Nina Patel
Head of Vendor Risk 
Aurora Health
[Attachment: Aurora_SCCS_Questions.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Aug 2029 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU-only processing questionnaire - initial ask

Nina — thanks for the questions and for attaching the questionnaire. Below are our consolidated responses for Aurora Health's pilot. I've included an evidence pack and links at the end.

1) EU-only processing and storage
- Commitment: Redwood will process and persist Aurora Health customer content exclusively in EU regions for the pilot. We will schedule the tenant in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) or eu-west-1 (Dublin) per your preference; configuration will be recorded in the tenant onboarding document and enforced by our routing policy.

2) Control plane and metadata
- The Redwood control plane (service orchestration, tenant metadata) runs on a separate, dedicated control plane that does not store customer content. Control-plane telemetry and operational logs are stored in the EU control plane when the account is configured for EU-only. We will include a contractual commitment in the SOW that control plane telemetry relevant to Aurora will be retained only within EU regions.

3) SCCs and contractual scope
- Redwood will execute the EU Commission SCCs addendum applicable at signing (we support the new SCCs template). For in-region processing, we will sign the SCCs and append a schedule that specifies processing locations and operator access constraints.

4) Operator access
- Access model: role-based human access with least-privilege. Operators requiring elevated access must request a break-glass with justification; each break-glass event generates an auditable ticket and session recording.
- We can provide redacted operator session logs and a time-bound list of individuals who have had emergency access. If Aurora requires per-person full audit traces, we can provide that under a separate evidence request and redaction agreement.

5) Backups, retention, and deletion proof
- Backups: secondary backups for pilot are stored in EU-only snapshot storage and encrypted with regionally scoped keys.
- Retention: baseline pilot retention = 30 days for backups; live data retention per tenant configurable (we recommend policy TTLs aligned to your retention requirements).
- Deletion proof: we provide object-level deletion events, snapshot purge logs, and an attestation of deletion. Upon request we will deliver a signed deletion attestation and a redacted log extract showing object identifiers and purge timestamps.

6) KMS and key management
- Options: (A) Redwood-managed regional CMK (default) or (B) customer-managed key (CMK) in region via AWS KMS (we provide instructions for key grants). For an Aurora CMK we will provide KM ARNs and required IAM principals to grant access.

Evidence and artifacts provided (attached):
- Operator_Access_Matrix.csv (roles + controls)
- Redwood_EU_Processing_Evidence.zip (redacted audit logs, config manifests, SCCs addendum template)
- Sample deletion attestation (PDF inside zip)

Next steps and timeline
- If the above is acceptable, we will: (1) sign SCCs addendum & SOW, (2) provision tenant in your preferred EU region, (3) provide the evidence pack and a 60‑minute technical walkthrough. We can deliver the signed attestation and redacted logs within 5 business days after SCCs execution.

DocuSign and links
- DocuSign MSA + SCCs: https://redwoodinference.app/docusign/MSA-Aurora-2029
- Technical runbook (internal): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SEC/EU+Processing+Runbook

Please let us know if you want the CMK option enabled for the pilot — if so we'll provide the IAM grant template and coordinate key creation. If you prefer, we can also provide a brief 30-minute session with our privacy engineer to walk through the evidence bundle.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: Operator_Access_Matrix.csv, Redwood_EU_Processing_Evidence.zip]
